Rashi on Berakhot 43b:10:1.hebrew: ולא היא - לא אמר רבא הלכתא כב"ה, אלא רב פפא אכסיף לפי שטעה, והשמיט עצמו בכך:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:10:1.english: And it is not so - Rava did not say that the halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel; rather, Rav Pappa was embarrassed because he had erred, and he extricated himself with this.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:1.hebrew: שמן ויין - זהו יין שלאחר המזון, ואין זה כוס של ברכה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:1.english: Oil and wine - This is wine [served] after the meal, and this is not the cup of blessing [for Grace after Meals].

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:2.hebrew: שמן בימינו - לפי שעליו מברך תחלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:2.english: Oil in his right hand - Because he recites the blessing over it first.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:3.english: He recites a blessing over the oil - [With the blessing:] "Who creates pleasant oil."

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:4.hebrew: חוזר ומברך על היין - כגון בחול, שאין היין קבע, ואין היין שלפני המזון פוטרו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:4.english: He then recites a blessing over the wine - Such as on a weekday, when wine is not an established fixture, and the wine [drunk] before the meal does not exempt it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:5.hebrew: וטחו בראש השמש - כדי שלא יצא בידיו מבושמות בשוק, שגנאי הוא לתלמיד חכם:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:11:5.english: And he smears it on the head of the servant - So that he does not go out with perfumed hands into the marketplace, as it is unbecoming for a Torah scholar.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:1.hebrew: שחשודים על משכב זכור - מבשמין עצמם כדי שיתאוו להם:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:1.english: Where they are suspected of homosexuality - They perfume themselves so that [others] will desire them.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:2.hebrew: ושערו כבגדו דמי - דלא שכיח ביה זיעה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:2.english: And his hair is considered like his clothing - For sweat is not common in it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:3.hebrew: ואמרי לה כגופו - דשכיח ביה זיעה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:13:3.english: And some say: Like his body - For sweat is common in it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:14:2.hebrew: דלא קביע ליה עידנא - שלא קבעו לו רבו קביעות ללמדו בלילה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:14:2.english: That he does not have a set time - That his teacher did not establish for him a fixed time to teach him at night.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:15:1.hebrew: בפנתא - אנפוני"א בלע"ז, שעל גבי הרגל:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:15:1.english: On the upper - Empeigne in Old French, which is on top of the foot.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:15:2.english: The sole - The heel [i.e., sole], which is called sole [in Old French].

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:15:3.english: During the rainy season - The mud covers it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:16:1.hebrew: אפי' היא אשתו - שאין הכל מכירין בה, וחושדין אותו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:16:1.english: Even if she is his wife - For not everyone recognizes her, and they will suspect him.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:18:1.english: Because they call him a transgressor - [Meaning,] he is being lazy.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:19:1.hebrew: בקדושא דבי שמשי - ששותה כוס של קידוש בשבת בלילה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:19:1.english: Through the Kiddush of twilight - That he drinks the cup of Kiddush on Shabbat night.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:1:1.hebrew: סמלק - יסמי"ן קורין לו בלשון ישמעאל, והוא מין עשב שיש בו שלש שורות של עלין זו למעלה מזו, ושלשה עלין לכל שורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:1:1.english: Simlak - They call it *yasmin* [jasmine] in the language of Ishmael [Arabic], and it is a type of herb that has three rows of leaves, one above the other, and three leaves to each row.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:1:2.hebrew: חלפי דימא - בושם שקורין אשפי"ג, והוא שבולת נרד, ועשוי כעין גבעולי פשתן, דאשכחן גבעולין דאיקרי עץ:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:1:2.english: Chalfei deyama - A spice that they call *espic* [spike lavender], and it is spikenard, and it is formed like stalks of flax, for we find stalks that are called 'tree'.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:2:1.english: Narcissus - [This is the] rose of Sharon, [according to] Halakhot Gedolot.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:2:2.english: Of a garden - That which grows in a garden.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:3:1.english: To adorn oneself - To derive pleasure.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:4:1.english: Like Lebanon - Whose leaves and blossoms emit fragrance.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:5:1.hebrew: יפה לו אומנתו - ואפי' בורסי, נאה לו אומנתו בעיניו. ועשה הקדוש ב"ה כן, שלא יחסר העולם אומנות:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:5:1.english: [God] made his craft pleasant for him - Even [for] a tanner, his craft is pleasant in his eyes. And the Holy One, blessed be He, did so, so that the world would not lack [a] craft:

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:6:1.hebrew: קורא - רך הגדל בדקל. תלה אותו לחזיר, והוא יגלגלנו באשפה, שזו היא אומנתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:6:1.english: Heart of palm - The tender [shoot] that grows on a palm tree. Hang it on a pig, and it will roll it in the refuse, for that is its trade.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:7:1.hebrew: אבוקה כשני בני אדם - לענין היוצא בלילה, דאמר מר: אל יצא אדם יחידי בלילה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:7:1.english: A torch is like two people - With regard to one who goes out at night, for the Master said: "A person should not go out alone at night."

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:7:2.hebrew: וירח כשלשה - ויש חלוק בין שנים לשלשה, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:7:2.english: And the moon is like three - And there is a distinction between two and three, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:7:3.english: To one, it appears - The demon [appears], and it harms him.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:8:1.hebrew: היא מוצאת והיא שלחה וגו' - ואילו בהדיא לא אמרה: ״אלו הסימנים של יהודה הם, ולו אני הרה״, אלא: ״לאיש אשר אלה לו אנכי הרה״ — אם יודה יודה, ואם לאו — אשרף ולא אלבין פניו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:8:1.english: She was being brought out, and she sent, etc. - Yet she did not say explicitly, "These tokens belong to Judah, and by him I am pregnant," but rather, "By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant" — [thinking:] if he admits [it], he will admit [it]; and if not, I will be burned and not humiliate him.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:9:1.hebrew: שמן והדס - בסוף הסעודה: שמן — לסוך ידיו להעביר זוהמת האוכלים, והדס — להריח, כמו שאמרנו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:9:1.english: Oil and myrtle - [This was] at the end of the meal: oil to anoint his hands to remove the grease of the food, and myrtle to smell, as we said.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:9:2.english: I will decide - In favor of Beit Shammai.

Rashi on Berakhot 43b:9:3.hebrew: זכינו לריחו ולסיכתו - כגון משחא כבישא, הלכך שמן עדיף:
Rashi on Berakhot 43b:9:3.english: We benefit from its fragrance and its anointing - For example, oil steeped [with spices]; therefore, oil is preferable.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:10:1.hebrew: הכי אמר רבא הלכתא כבית הלל ולא היא לאשתמוטי נפשיה הוא דקא עביד - כך כתוב בספרים שלנו ובפירוש רש"י, אבל רב אלפס פסק כרבא — משמע שלא היה גורס בספרו "ולא היא" וכו':
Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:10:1.english: "Rava said the following: The halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel. And that is not so; he did [this only] to extricate himself" - So it is written in our texts and in Rashi's commentary. However, Rav Alfas [the Rif] ruled in accordance with Rava, which implies that he did not have the reading "And that is not so, etc." in his text.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:2:1.hebrew: האי מאן דמורח באתרוגא וחבוש' מברך וכו' - ודוקא כשמריח בהם, אבל אם בא לאכול מהם — אין לברך ברכת ריח, כי אם ברכת אכילה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:2:1.english: "One who smells an etrog or a quince recites, etc." - And [this applies] specifically when one smells them; but if one comes to eat them, one does not recite the blessing over fragrance, but only the blessing over eating.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:9:1.hebrew: שמן והדס - האי שמן להריח הוא, דאי להעביר הזוהמא — הא אמרינן בפרק אלו דברים (לקמן ברכות נג.) דאין מברכין עליו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43b:9:1.english: "Oil and myrtle" - This oil is [meant] for smelling; for if [it were] to remove the filth, behold, we say in chapter Elu Devarim (below, Berakhot 53a) that one does not recite a blessing over it.
